description: The objective of this course is to introduce the mathematical foundation of stochastic processes. It is intended for students with strong mathematical inclinations and motivation. The emphasis will be on rigour, depth, and conceptual understanding. The contents of this course will consist of those in the regular course (MA3238/ST3236), developed in greater mathematical depth, and the following additional topics: random walks and electrical networks, discrete-time martingales, stochastic processes on graphs. The course will also cover various special classes of stochastic processes such as percolation and random graphs, spin systems and interacting particle systems.
